summary: Trade policy is back. On Nov 25 USTR proposed Section 301 excess-capacity tariffs on 14 economies (China +20%, plus Taiwan, Korea, Japan, the EU and India), landing on top of a renewed AI / chip sell-off (Kospi -6.2%, NVDA about -6% pre-market). The Fed's hiking path is the other main risk: core PCE rose to 3.3% and Q3 GDP was revised to 4.3%, and a Dec 9 hike is priced at 100%. Oil stays near 3-month lows despite Hormuz incidents ahead of OPEC+ Nov 29.

risks.title: Section 301 excess-capacity tariffs on 14 economies
risks.status: Nov 25: USTR determined that 14 economies (China, EU, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan, India) burden US commerce through structural excess capacity, and proposed tariffs; China faces an extra 20% on top of the 2018 25% (reportedly 40% if the truce fails). Mexico and Norway were left out for now. Other rates are due in a Federal Register notice; public hearings come first, so duties may not take effect until January. The new duties do not stack on the July forced-labor tariffs or on car / steel / aluminum tariffs (AP)
risks.market_pricing: Nov 25 pre-market: Nasdaq 100 futures -3.2%, S&P futures -2.0%; Kospi -6.16%, Nikkei -2.78%; SOXX indicated -5% at 122.18
risks.impact: Final rates at or above the proposals, or Chinese retaliation, would extend the semis de-rating and add to goods inflation (more Fed hikes); softened rates or carve-outs after hearings would relieve Asia-linked chip supply chains

risks.title: Fed hiking path and Fed leadership (Chair Warsh)
risks.status: Nov 25: October core PCE 3.3% y/y (vs 3.2% expected, highest since Nov 2023), +0.3% m/m in line; headline 3.8%; Q3 GDP revised to 4.3% (vs 3.5% expected). FedWatch about 97% for a 25bp Dec 9 hike and about 60% for another in January (Investing.com via mlq.ai). Beige Book 14:00 ET. Nov 24: Conference Board confidence jumped to 103.3 (vs about 92 expected), supporting hike pricing; media cite about 95% for a 25bp Dec 9 hike and 4-5% for 50bp; Williams (Nov 23) said persistent inflation still points to tighter policy, data-dependent. October PCE and Q3 GDP Nov 25. Nov 23: Treasury Secretary Bessent warned over the weekend that policymakers risk overtightening; Polymarket prices a Dec 9 hike at about 91% (down from 98% on Nov 12); NY Fed's Williams speaks 16:00 ET; October PCE Nov 25. Nov 20: Cook said waiting longer 'risks getting behind the curve'. Held 3.75-4.00% on Oct 28 (Cook and Hammack dissented for a hike). Nov 18 minutes: 'almost all participants' see further hikes as likely appropriate, and 'a couple' would consider more than 25bp; Waller kept 50bp on the table. Nov 19: claims 203k (above ~197k), Philly Fed 6.3 with prices paid 58.2. Nov 20: Waller speaks in Santiago at 08:25 ET (he has said 50bp 'should be considered') and Cook (October hike dissenter) at 12:15 ET; Treasury yields fell another 7bp pre-market on haven demand. November CPI lands after the Dec 9 decision
risks.odds: Dec 9 hike 100%, implied 4.15% (+27bp) (fed funds futures, Nov 23); Polymarket hike ~91% (via Yahoo Finance, Nov 23); Kalshi 25bp 91% / larger 8% (via Capp Notes, Nov 18); FedWatch 69% for 50bp of hikes by end-January (via Yahoo Finance, Nov 18)
risks.market_pricing: Nov 19 midday: 13-week 4.153% (3-month high), 5Y 4.877%, 10Y 5.06% (+93.7bp over 1 year, 98th 10-year pct), 10Y real 2.89%; DXY 103.83 (3-month high); gold 3,682 (3-month low)
risks.impact: 50bp talk or hot data would push the 10Y back toward 5.3% and hit long-duration tech, small caps and housing; a 25bp-and-gradual message with softer data would ease yields and help rate-sensitive groups

risks.title: AI trade: Anthropic IPO, Nvidia leadership, export controls and AI-debt worries
risks.status: Nov 25: the sell-off went global: Kospi -6.16% (SK Hynix -11.1%, Samsung -9.9%), Nikkei -2.8%, ASML -3%; pre-market NVDA about -6% (about $146), AMD -6.9%, MU -8%, ANT about $77.7 (below its $83 IPO); Dell -6.9% despite raising guidance and a record $132.3B AI backlog (margin worries). Nov 24: the relief rally reversed: NVDA -5% to -8%, AMD about -10%, MU about -8%, SOXX about -9% intraday; HPE -11% to -16% after guiding FY27 Cloud & AI operating margin to about 14% from 18.4%; ADI about -15% on guidance; ANT briefly below its $83 IPO price (insider sales to underwriters; MSCI inclusion Nov 30); a US blacklisting of an Alibaba-owned firm was reported. Dell reports after the close. Nov 23: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, effective immediately (Trump had publicly urged it); the board's independent investigation continues and a National Security and Export Control Committee was formed. NVDA jumped about 30% at the open after -40% in a month; SOXX gapped +15%. Nov 20: S&P -3.7%, NVDA -13.7%, semis' worst week since 2001; the AMD Hunterbrook short report (China exposure) remains disputed. Nov 20 pre-market: ANT down about 10% from its $97.17 close (IPO $83); Intuit about -10% on soft Q2 guidance; AVGO about -3% on a report Google may buy HBM directly; MU/WDC about -4%; NVDA on a six-day decline; Nasdaq 100 futures -1.3% to -1.7%. Nov 19: Anthropic (ANT) priced at $83 (above $70-78) and opened at $111.50 at 11:50 ET (+34%, record $81.3B raise, valuation above $1.5T), then faded toward about $97. Chip stocks erased their gains after the debut: AMD -8% on a short report citing China ties (per Yahoo's live blog), Nvidia and Broadcom turned red. Earlier: Nvidia beat and raised under interim CEO Kress but fell five straight days; Huang had resigned Nov 12 (since reversed); the FOMC minutes flagged opaque AI-related debt; the Commerce AI-chip licensing rule; Nvidia's general counsel testifies to House committees Dec 2
risks.market_pricing: Nov 23 09:45: SOXX 137.44 (+11.7%, opened 142.18), QQQ 645.38 (+6.2%), SMH +13.7% on the day but still -8.2pp vs SPY over 1 month. Nov 19 midday: SOXX 140.02 after a 148.59 high (a 7.4% intraday swing), QQQ 652.24 after 676.46; SMH -11.8pp vs SPY over 1 month and -13.5pp over 3 months
risks.impact: If capital rotates into ANT, a credit event at an AI-debt borrower or tighter export rules would extend the semis de-rating below the 136 higher low; stabilizing ANT trading and strong AI earnings (Intuit and Keysight tonight) would let semis rebuild from support

risks.title: US-Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz
risks.status: Nov 24: three tankers reportedly struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and Treasury Secretary Bessent announced new Iran sanctions on more than two dozen exchange houses and front companies (per HDFC Sky, not confirmed by a wire); Brent still fell to about 86.8, a 3-month low. Nov 22-23: Trump said over the weekend that strikes on Iran could resume next year if talks fail (per Blye Sheet); the Houthis claimed an attack on a Saudi refinery on Sunday (Reuters via Yahoo, unconfirmed); Libya's output fell about 350k b/d on a pipeline disruption. Brent still fell to 87.92 (-5%), a 3-month low. Nov 19-20: the NYT reports Trump is weighing fresh strikes on Iran, with Netanyahu pushing a 4-7 day campaign; no decision yet (Trump told Axios he is not rushing). About 14 Iranian attacks on vessels near Hormuz in the first 19 days of November (UK maritime count via Bloomberg); a tanker was hit near Oman and a Riyadh skyscraper damaged. Brent still fell to 88.96 on Nov 20 pre-market. Nov 19: Bloomberg reports that Iran has intensified tanker attacks in Hormuz since October, with at least two seafarers missing this week, even as oil slides. Iran claims ships struck mines without offering evidence. Hormuz shipments are reported back near pre-war levels. Nov 17-18: the US struck an IRGC site on Qeshm Island; Iranian drones targeted bases in Kuwait and Bahrain (intercepted); an ADNOC ship was hit (1 missing, 11 injured). Trump: 'we don't need a deal with Iran'. The US and Israel are reportedly debating larger action
risks.odds: No current ceasefire market found; Polymarket priced the ceasefire holding through Nov 2 at 78% on Nov 3, down 20 points after US strikes (Rio Times)
risks.market_pricing: Nov 19: WTI 83.34, Brent 90.04 (-2.1%, -17% over 1 month), near 3-month lows despite the attacks; OVX 49.9 (Nov 17, 80th pct)
risks.impact: A successful hit on Gulf export infrastructure or renewed large-scale strikes would send Brent back above $100 and add to inflation and hike pricing; a signed deal would push Brent toward the high $70s and help consumers, transports and rate-sensitive stocks while hurting energy and defense

risks.title: China-Taiwan tensions, chip export controls and US-China trade truce
risks.status: Nov 25: the US Section 301 excess-capacity proposals include China (+20%), Taiwan, Korea and Japan (see section-301-tariffs); a Chinese response is the next risk. Nov 23: China eased margin requirements and Taiwan and South Korea introduced market-stabilizing measures after last week's chip rout (per Blye Sheet). The Trump-Xi meetings in Shenzhen (Nov 18-19) ended with little change on chips, rare earths or tariffs; leaders sidestepped a question on Nvidia's Huang. China vowed countermeasures to the US AI-chip licensing rule. The trade truce runs to Jan 10; Trump and Xi are expected to meet again at the G20 in Florida in December. Taiwan curbed short selling Nov 9
risks.market_pricing: SOXX 35.7% below its 52-week high; AMD -8% Nov 19 on China-ties concerns
risks.impact: Chinese retaliation (rare-earth curbs, probes of US chipmakers) or Taiwan drills would hit semis first; a truce extension or eased licensing would support a semis rebound

risks.title: US government funding / shutdown risk and debt limit
risks.status: The stopgap funds the government through Dec 11. Leaders in both parties reportedly back another short-term stopgap past the lame-duck session; options are an omnibus/minibuses, a CR into January-March 2027, or both. The debt limit could bind as soon as February 2027. The US has had three funding lapses since October 2025
risks.impact: A December lapse would delay economic data the Fed needs before Dec 9-era decisions and dent Q4 growth; a clean CR into the new Congress removes it until the debt-limit fight

risks.title: CMS anti-fraud rule for managed care (Medicare Advantage)
risks.status: CMS proposed an anti-fraud rule (CRUSH) on Nov 18; UnitedHealth fell another 5% on Nov 19, about -18% over five days, and health care led Thursday's losses
risks.market_pricing: XLV -1.75% Nov 19, -5.2% over 5 days, but still +7.8pp vs SPY over 3 months
risks.impact: A broad final rule would cut managed-care margins and weigh on the Dow and health-care leadership; a narrowed rule or long comment period would let the group recover

risks.title: OPEC+ output policy (2027 quotas)
risks.status: Nov 25: Brent about $87.5-89 ahead of the Nov 29 virtual meeting; reports of disagreement over Iraq's capacity baseline; Eurasia Group sees Brent in the lower half of $80-100. OPEC+ kept December targets unchanged on Nov 1. All 21 members meet Nov 29 to set the 2027 production framework, shaped by a capacity audit due mid-November; about 2M b/d of cuts cover most members through end-2026. Gulf exports have run at 60-80% of normal because of the Iran war. Goldman's December Brent forecast is $105; the IEA sees a Q4 surplus
risks.market_pricing: Brent 90.04, far below Goldman's $105 December forecast; WTI near its lowest since late August
risks.impact: Restoring more capacity in 2027 would extend oil's slide and hurt energy stocks while helping inflation; extended restraint would put a floor under oil

risks.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping
risks.status: A Houthi attack reportedly damaged Aramco offices in Riyadh (reported Nov 9, not confirmed elsewhere); Saudi Arabia warned its Yanbu Red Sea oil hub could be targeted (Nov 6); no new incident found Nov 13-19. Trump tied a US-Saudi nuclear deal to Saudi Arabia joining the Abraham Accords (Nov 18)
risks.market_pricing: No visible Red Sea premium; Brent near a 3-month low
risks.impact: A hit on Saudi export infrastructure (Yanbu) would be a major oil shock; calm keeps the focus on Iran

risks.title: Israel government formation after the Oct 27 election
risks.status: Herzog handed Gadi Eisenkot the mandate on Nov 8; he has 28 days (extendable by 14) and is open to including Netanyahu, who stays caretaker PM. CENTCOM's chief met Israel's military chief Nov 18 amid talk of renewed action on Iran
risks.impact: An Eisenkot-led or unity government would likely be more cautious on Iran (mildly bearish oil and defense); a failed mandate extends caretaker uncertainty

risks.title: Russia-Ukraine war and peace talks
risks.status: US-brokered trilateral talks resumed in Abu Dhabi Nov 10-11, focused on a post-war European security framework; Russia still insists on all of Donbas; no outcome reported since. Putin's reported attendance at Shenzhen was not confirmed
risks.odds: Peace talks by Dec 31 90%, ceasefire by Dec 31 9.5%, by Mar 31 2027 23.5% (Polymarket via Rio Times, early Nov)
risks.impact: Real progress would be mildly bearish for defense and European gas; a collapse keeps the defense theme supported
